name: opencode 2.x
description: Registers Polter's MCP server with opencode 2.x by editing ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json -- `opencode mcp add` is an interactive wizard, so this one edits a config file, refusing outright if it cannot parse what is there. Needs python3 for that. Mirrors Polter's skills into ~/.config/opencode/skills/polter-* -- unless they are already under ~/.claude/skills, which opencode reads too: then that is the one copy, and none go here. This is the plugin for opencode 2.x only; opencode 1.x has its own, and neither serves the other's version.

skills.title: Install skills as well
skills.description: yes mirrors Polter's skills into this host's skills directory. Polter's skill_read has to be thought of first; a host's own skills are matched against what the user asked for, which is the whole difference. no registers the MCP server and takes back the polter-* skills an earlier yes installed; skills you wrote yourself are never touched.

rules.title: Write Polter's note into this CLI's rules file
rules.description: yes writes a marked block into the user-level rules file (never a project one) saying that what an agent prints reaches nobody, and pointing at the operating-a-terminal skill. It is there because a skill is matched against what the user asked for and nothing matches "you have just finished a task": on real records, 71 tasks produced 15 done reports. Everything outside the markers is left untouched, and no takes the block back out. For opencode the file is ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md; opencode 2.x reads no CLAUDE.md, so writing it hides nothing of yours. The same file the opencode 1.x plugin writes: both are the one opencode, and only one of the two plugins is turned on.
